title.zh: 卷2 本紀二 太宗本紀一
title.raw: 卷2 本紀二 太宗本紀一

sentences.zh: 太宗應天興國弘德彰武寬溫仁聖睿孝敬敏昭定隆道顯功文皇帝，諱皇太極，太祖第八子，母孝慈高皇后。

translations.literal: Taizong, the Emperor of Responding to Heaven, Raising the State, Magnifying Virtue, Displaying Martial Prowess, Broad Kindness, Benevolent Sagacity, Wise Filial Piety, Respectful Diligence, Brightly Settled, Lofty in the Way, and Distinguished in Achievement — taboo name Huang Taiji; eighth son of Taizu; mother Empress Xiaoci Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, posthumously honored with the full title of a sage emperor who answered Heaven and exalted the realm, was known in life by the taboo name Huang Taiji. He was Taizu Nurhaci’s eighth son, born to Empress Xiaoci Gao.

sentences.zh: 上儀表奇偉，聰睿絕倫，顏如渥丹，嚴寒不栗。

translations.literal: The Emperor’s bearing and appearance were singular and imposing; his intelligence and keen insight were without peer; his complexion was like moist cinnabar; in severe cold he did not shiver.
translations.idiomatic: He was striking in stature and presence, with an intellect that outshone all around him. His face held a deep, ruddy flush, and even in bitter cold he never so much as shivered.

sentences.zh: 長益神勇，善騎射，性耽典籍，諮覽弗倦，仁孝寬惠，廓然有大度。

translations.literal: As he grew he gained ever more divine courage; he was skilled at riding and shooting; by nature he delighted in the classics and inquired into them without tiring; humane, filial, generous, and kindly — open and great in breadth of mind.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he grew ever bolder and more formidable, a master of horse and bow who could lose himself for hours in books without fatigue. He was known for kindness, filial devotion, and a magnanimity that seemed to have no limit.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，儲嗣未定。

translations.literal: Taizu died; the heir was not yet fixed.
translations.idiomatic: When Nurhaci died, no successor had yet been named.

sentences.zh: 代善與其子岳託、薩哈廉以上才德冠世，與諸貝勒議請嗣位。

translations.literal: Daisan, together with his sons Yuetuo and Sahalian, held that in talent and virtue the Emperor surpassed the age; with the various beile they deliberated and requested that he succeed to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Daisan and his sons Yuetuo and Sahalian declared that Huang Taiji’s talent and virtue stood above all others of their day. Together with the other princes they pressed him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 上辭再三，久之乃許。

translations.literal: The Emperor declined again and again; only after a long time did he consent.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Taiji refused repeatedly, and only after prolonged urging did he at last accept.

sentences.zh: 辛未，誓告天地，以行正道，循禮義，敦友愛，盡公忠，勖諸大貝勒等。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, he swore and announced to Heaven and Earth that he would walk the upright path, follow ritual and righteousness, deepen fraternal affection, and fulfill public loyalty, exhorting the great beile and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day he took oath before Heaven and Earth to govern by the straight path—honoring ritual, nurturing brotherhood among the princes, and serving the public good—and he charged the senior beile to do the same.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，諭漢官民有私計遁逃及令奸細往來者，雖首告勿論，後惟已逃被獲者論死。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu, he announced to Han officials and commoners: those who privately plotted flight or ordered spies to come and go — even if they confessed first, it would not be discussed; hereafter only those already fled and then captured would be sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day he proclaimed to Han officials and subjects that anyone who schemed to flee or traded in intelligence with the enemy would find no mercy in confession alone. Henceforth only fugitives who were caught after escaping would face execution.

sentences.zh: 丙子，諭曰：「工築之興，有妨農務，前以城郭邊牆，事關守禦，有勞民力，良非得已。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, he announced, saying: “The rise of labor and construction hinders agricultural affairs. Previously, because city walls and frontier ramparts concerned defense, the burden on the people’s strength was unavoidable.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day he issued an edict: “Public works have been cutting into the farming season. Walls and border fortifications were a matter of defense, and conscripting labor for them was a painful necessity.

sentences.zh: 茲後止葺頹壞，不復興築，俾民專勤南畝。

translations.literal: Hereafter we shall only repair what is ruined and collapsed, and not raise new construction again, so that the people may devote themselves solely to tilling the southern fields.
translations.idiomatic: From now on we will mend only what has fallen into ruin and build nothing new, so that the people can give their full attention to the fields.”

sentences.zh: 滿洲、漢人，毋或異視，訟獄差徭，務使均一。

translations.literal: Manchu and Han — let none be viewed differently; in lawsuits, corvée, and levies, see that all are made uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Manchu and Han alike are to be treated as one people; litigation, labor service, and taxes must be applied evenly to all.”

sentences.zh: 貝勒屬下人，毋許邊外行獵。

translations.literal: Persons under the beile are not permitted to hunt beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: No subject of a beile may hunt beyond the border marches.”

sentences.zh: 市稅為國費所出，聽其通商貿易，私往外國及漏稅者罪之。

translations.literal: Market duties are drawn for state expenses; let trade and commerce pass freely; those who privately go to foreign states or evade tax shall be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Market tolls fund the state treasury—trade may flow freely, but anyone who deals abroad in secret or dodges the tax will be punished.”

sentences.zh: 」丁丑，令漢人與滿洲分屯別居。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, he ordered Han and Manchu to dwell in separate encampments.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day he ordered Han Chinese and Manchu to live in separate settlements.

sentences.zh: 先是漢人十三壯丁為一莊，給滿官為奴。

translations.literal: Previously, thirteen able-bodied Han men formed one estate and were given to Manchu officials as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Until then, every thirteen adult Han men had been grouped into an estate and assigned as bondsmen to Manchu officers.

sentences.zh: 至是，每備御止留八人，餘悉編為民戶，處以別屯，擇漢官廉正者理之。

translations.literal: At this time, for each defending officer only eight were retained; the rest were all enrolled as civilian households, placed in separate encampments, and honest Han officials were chosen to administer them.
translations.idiomatic: Now each garrison officer was allowed only eight such men; the remainder were registered as free households in separate villages under the supervision of upright Han officials.

sentences.zh: 設八固山額真，分領八旗。

translations.literal: Eight gushan ejen were established to command the Eight Banners in division.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed eight gushan ejen—banner commanders—to lead the Eight Banners.

sentences.zh: 以納穆泰為正黃旗固山額真，額駙達爾漢為鑲黃旗固山額真，額駙和碩圖為正紅旗固山額真，博爾晉為鑲紅旗固山額真，額駙顧三泰為鑲藍旗固山額真，托博輝為正藍旗固山額真，徹爾格為鑲白旗固山額真，喀克篤禮為正白旗固山額真。

translations.literal: Namutai was made gushan ejen of the Plain Yellow Banner; Prince-Consort Dalhan of the Bordered Yellow; Prince-Consort Hosotu of the Plain Red; Boringjin of the Bordered Red; Prince-Consort Gursan of the Bordered Blue; Tobohoi of the Plain Blue; Cergei of the Bordered White; Kakduri of the Plain White.
translations.idiomatic: Namutai took the Plain Yellow Banner; Prince-Consort Dalhan the Bordered Yellow; Prince-Consort Hosotu the Plain Red; Boringjin the Bordered Red; Prince-Consort Gursan the Bordered Blue; Tobohoi the Plain Blue; Cergei the Bordered White; and Kakduri the Plain White.

sentences.zh: 又設十六大臣，贊理庶政，聽八旗訟獄。

translations.literal: Sixteen ministers were also established to assist in governing the myriad affairs and to hear lawsuits of the Eight Banners.
translations.idiomatic: He also created sixteen ministers to help govern civil affairs and adjudicate disputes within the Eight Banners.

sentences.zh: 又設十六大臣，參理訟獄，行軍駐防則遣之。

translations.literal: Sixteen more ministers were established to join in handling lawsuits; on campaign or garrison duty they were dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Another sixteen ministers were named to share judicial duties and to accompany armies in the field or on frontier station.

sentences.zh: 乙未，蒙古科爾沁土謝圖汗奧巴遣使來吊。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, Ooba, Tüsiyetü Khan of the Mongol Khorchin, sent envoys to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day Ooba, the Tüsiyetü Khan of Khorchin, dispatched mourners to the court.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己酉，以蒙古喀爾喀札魯特部敗盟殺掠，私通於明，命大貝勒代善等率精兵萬人討之，先貽書聲其罪，上送至蒲河山而還。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, winter, on the day jiyou — because the Khalkha Zhaluut of Mongolia had broken the alliance, killed, plundered, and secretly communicated with the Ming — the Emperor ordered the great beile Daisan and others to lead ten thousand picked troops to punish them; first a letter was sent proclaiming their crimes; the Emperor escorted them to Puhe Mountain and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on jiyou, learning that the Zhaluut Khalkha had broken faith, raided Qing territory, and conspired with the Ming, he sent Great Beile Daisan at the head of ten thousand elite troops to chastise them. A written indictment of their crimes went ahead of the army; the Emperor rode with the host to Puhe Mountain, then turned back.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，別遣楞額禮、阿山率輕兵六百入喀爾喀巴林地，以張軍勢。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, separately he dispatched Lenggeri and Ashan with six hundred light troops into the Khalkha forest lands to magnify the army’s presence.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day he sent Lenggeri and Ashan with six hundred light cavalry into the Khalkha woodlands to feign a larger force.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，科爾沁土謝圖汗奧巴及代達爾漢等十四貝勒各遣使來吊。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Ooba, Tüsiyetü Khan of the Khorchin, and fourteen beile including Prince-Consort Daidalhan each sent envoys to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day Ooba of Khorchin and fourteen beile, among them Prince-Consort Daidalhan, each sent delegations of condolence.

sentences.zh: 達硃戶征卦爾察部，獲其人口牲畜以歸。

translations.literal: Dazhu led a campaign against the Gorcha and returned with captives, people, and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhu marched against the Gorcha and returned with prisoners, herds, and booty.

sentences.zh: 明寧遠巡撫袁崇煥遣李喇嘛及都司傅有爵等來吊，並賀即位。

translations.literal: Yuan Chonghuan, Ming pacification commissioner of Ningyuan, sent the Lama Li and the director Fu Youjue and others to offer condolences and to congratulate him on assuming the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chonghuan, Ming governor of Ningyuan, sent Lama Li and Director Fu Youjue with others both to mourn Nurhaci and to congratulate Huang Taiji on his accession.

sentences.zh: 甲子，大貝勒代善等大破札魯特，斬其貝勒鄂爾齋圖，獲貝勒巴克及其二子並拉什希布等十四貝勒而還。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, the great beile Daisan and the rest utterly defeated the Zhaluut, beheaded their beile Orchitu, and returned having captured Beile Bak and his two sons together with Rashib and thirteen other beile.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day Daisan’s army shattered the Zhaluut, slew their beile Orchitu, and came home with Bak, his two sons, Rashib, and thirteen other beile as prisoners.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛未，上發瀋陽迎大貝勒代善，師次鐵嶺樊河界。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day xinwei, the Emperor set out from Mukden to welcome the great beile Daisan; the army halted at the border of Tieling and the Fan River.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on xinwei day, Huang Taiji left Mukden to meet Great Beile Daisan’s returning column and camped at the Tieling–Fan River line.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，行飲至禮，論功，頒賚將士。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, he performed the ritual of drinking to the completion of the campaign, assessed merit, and bestowed rewards on officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day he held the victory feast, reviewed achievements, and distributed rewards among the troops.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，上還瀋陽。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, the Emperor returned to Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day he returned to Mukden.

sentences.zh: 察哈爾阿喇克綽忒部貝勒圖爾濟率百戶來歸。

translations.literal: Turgen, beile of the Chakhar Alakötü, led a hundred households to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Turgen, beile of the Chakhar Alakötü branch, came in with a hundred households.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，遣方吉納、溫塔石偕李喇嘛往報袁崇煥，且遺書曰：「頃停息干戈，遣使弔賀，來者以禮，故遣官陳謝。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, he dispatched Fangjina and Wentashi together with Lama Li to report to Yuan Chonghuan, and also sent a letter saying: “We have lately ceased arms and sent envoys to mourn and congratulate; you have treated the coming party with courtesy, and so we send officials to express thanks.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day he sent Fangjina and Wentashi with Lama Li to answer Yuan Chonghuan, enclosing a letter: “We have laid down the sword for the moment and sent envoys in mourning and congratulation; you received them with propriety, and we therefore send these officers to thank you.

sentences.zh: 昔皇考往寧遠時，曾致璽書言和，未獲回答。

translations.literal: In former days, when my late father went to Ningyuan, he once sent a sealed letter proposing peace but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: When my late father marched on Ningyuan he once wrote under seal proposing peace, and never received an answer.

sentences.zh: 如其修好，答書以實，勿事文飾。

translations.literal: If you wish to make peace in good faith, reply in truth and do not dress the matter in fine phrases.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly desire peace, answer plainly—do not cloak your words in ornament.”

sentences.zh: 」崇煥不以聞，而令我使繼還。

translations.literal: Chonghuan did not report this upward, but ordered our envoys to return at once.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghuan never forwarded the letter to his court; he simply sent the Qing envoys home.

sentences.zh: 卓禮克圖貝勒之子衛徵巴拜手巂其家屬來歸。

translations.literal: Weijengbabai, son of the Jorčitu beile, came leading his household in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Weijengbabai, son of a Jorčitu beile, arrived with his entire family to swear allegiance.

sentences.zh: 科爾沁貝勒青巴圖魯桑阿爾齋、台吉滿珠什哩各繼鞍馬牛羊來吊。

translations.literal: The Khorchin beile Čingbatu Sang’arsan and the taiji Manjusiri each in turn sent saddled horses, cattle, and sheep as mourning gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Khorchin beile Čingbatu Sang’arsan and the taiji Manjusiri each sent horses, cattle, and sheep as condolence offerings.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚子，禁與蒙古諸籓售賣兵仗。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day gengzi, the sale of weapons to the various Mongol vassals was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengzi day, he banned the sale of arms to Mongol tributaries.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，黑龍江人來朝貢。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, people of the Amur came to court to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day delegations from the Amur valley presented tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 二月己亥，以書招諭蒙古奈曼部袞出斯巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day jihai, a letter was sent summoning Günüsibaatur of the Mongol Naiman.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jihai day, he wrote to summon Günüsibaatur of the Naiman Mongols.

sentences.zh: 三月壬申，阿敏等克朝鮮義州，別遣兵搗鐵山，明守將毛文龍遁走。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day renshen, Amin and others captured the Korean Uiju; separately troops were sent to strike Tieshan, and the Ming commander Mao Wenlong fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renshen day, Amin took the Korean town of Uiju while a detached force struck Tieshan and drove off the Ming general Mao Wenlong.

sentences.zh: 又克安州，進至平壤城，渡大同江。

translations.literal: They also took Anzhou, advanced to Pyongyang, and crossed the Taedong River.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Anzhou, pushed on to Pyongyang, and crossed the Taedong.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮國王李倧遣使迎師。

translations.literal: The King of Korea, Li Zong, sent envoys to welcome the army.
translations.idiomatic: King Li Zong of Korea sent envoys to greet the invaders.

sentences.zh: 阿敏等數其七罪，仍遣使趣和。

translations.literal: Amin and the rest enumerated seven crimes against him and still sent envoys urging peace.
translations.idiomatic: Amin recited seven counts against the king and nevertheless dispatched messengers pressing for settlement.

sentences.zh: 倧懼，率妻子遁江華島，其長子李𣳫遁全州。

translations.literal: Li Zong, in fear, led his wife and children in flight to Ganghwa Island; his eldest son Li Hui fled to Jeonju.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Li Zong fled with his family to Ganghwa Island while his heir Li Hui withdrew to Jeonju.

sentences.zh: 阿敏復遣副將劉興祚入島面諭倧。

translations.literal: Amin again sent the deputy commander Liu Xingzuo into the island to instruct Li Zong face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Amin sent Deputy Commander Liu Xingzuo to the island to parley with the king in person.

sentences.zh: 倧遣其族弟原昌君李覺獻馬百匹、虎豹皮百、錦苧各四百、布一萬五千。

translations.literal: Li Zong sent his clansman Wonchang-gun Li Jue to present a hundred horses, a hundred tiger and leopard pelts, four hundred each of brocade and ramie, and fifteen thousand bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The king sent his kinsman Wonchang-gun Li Jue with a hundred horses, a hundred tiger and leopard skins, four hundred lengths each of brocade and ramie, and fifteen thousand bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 庚子，與朝鮮盟，定議罷兵。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, a treaty was made with Korea and it was decided to cease hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day Korea and the Qing concluded a treaty and the armies stood down.

sentences.zh: 壬申，明袁崇煥遣杜明忠偕方吉納等以書來，並李喇嘛書，欲釋恨修好。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, Yuan Chonghuan of the Ming sent Du Mingzhong together with Fangjina and others with letters, including one from Lama Li, wishing to set aside enmity and restore peace.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day Yuan Chonghuan sent Du Mingzhong with Fangjina and others, bearing letters—including one from Lama Li—seeking to bury the feud and reopen relations.

sentences.zh: 惟請減金幣之數，而以我稱兵朝鮮為疑。

translations.literal: He only asked that the amount of gold and goods be reduced, and he harbored suspicion because we had raised arms against Korea.
translations.idiomatic: He asked only that the tribute in gold and goods be lowered, and he professed doubt over the Korean campaign.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，阿敏等遣使奏捷。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, Amin and the rest sent envoys to report victory.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day Amin’s staff dispatched messengers announcing victory.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，命留滿洲兵一千、蒙古兵二千防義州，滿洲兵三百、蒙古兵一千防鎮江城。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, he ordered a thousand Manchu troops and two thousand Mongol troops left to garrison Uiju, and three hundred Manchu and a thousand Mongol to garrison Zhenjiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day he left a thousand Manchu and two thousand Mongol troops at Uiju, and three hundred Manchu with a thousand Mongol at Zhenjiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 並諭李倧曰：「我留兵義州者，防毛文龍耳。

translations.literal: He also instructed Li Zong, saying: “The troops I leave at Uiju are to guard against Mao Wenlong alone.
translations.idiomatic: He told Li Zong plainly: “The garrison at Uiju is aimed only at Mao Wenlong.

sentences.zh: 」阿敏等旋師，以李覺歸。

translations.literal: Amin and the rest withdrew the army and returned with Li Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Amin then marched home, bringing Li Jue with him.

sentences.zh: 夏四月甲辰，遺袁崇煥書曰：「釋恨修好，固所原也。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the day jiachen, a letter was sent to Yuan Chonghuan saying: “To set aside hatred and restore peace is indeed what we desire.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on jiachen day, he wrote to Yuan Chonghuan: “Peace is what we want as well.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮自尊輕我，納我叛亡，我遲之數年，彼不知悔，是以興討。

translations.literal: Korea held itself proud and slighted us, harbored our fugitives and deserters; we waited several years, yet they did not know repentance — therefore we raised the punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Korea treated us with contempt, sheltered our runaways, and after years of forbearance showed no remorse—so we went to war.

sentences.zh: 天誘其衷，我軍克捷。

translations.literal: Heaven guided their hearts; our army achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven favored us, and our arms prevailed.

sentences.zh: 今已和矣，而爾詭言修好，仍遣哨卒偵視，修葺城堡。

translations.literal: Now peace has been made, yet you speak of good relations while still sending scouts to spy and repairing your fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: That quarrel is settled, yet you talk of friendship while your scouts probe our lines and your walls rise higher.

sentences.zh: 我國將帥，實以此致疑。

translations.literal: Our generals in truth take this as cause for suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Our commanders, with reason, do not trust you.

sentences.zh: 夫講信修睦，必藉物以成禮，我豈貪而利此，使爾國力不支？

translations.literal: To speak faith and cultivate harmony, material things are needed to complete the ritual — would I be greedy and profit by this, so that your state’s strength could not bear it?
translations.idiomatic: Courtesy between states requires gifts to seal the bond—do you imagine I crave your silver so keenly that I would beggar your treasury?

sentences.zh: 可減其半。

translations.literal: It may be reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: Halve the sum, then.

sentences.zh: 歲時餽答，當如前議，則兩國之福也。

translations.literal: Annual exchanges of gifts should follow the prior agreement; then the fortune of both states.
translations.idiomatic: Let the yearly tribute follow what we already agreed, and both realms will prosper.”

sentences.zh: 」書成，聞崇煥方築塔山、大凌河、錦州等城，遂罷遣使，而以書付杜明忠還。

translations.literal: When the letter was finished, it was learned that Chonghuan was building Tashan, Dalinghe, Jinzhou, and other cities; the dispatch of envoys was therefore halted, and the letter was given to Du Mingzhong to carry back.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly was the letter sealed when word came that Chonghuan was fortifying Tashan, Dalinghe, and Jinzhou; Huang Taiji canceled the embassy and sent the missive back with Du Mingzhong alone.

sentences.zh: 更責崇煥曰：「兩國修好，當分定疆域。

translations.literal: He further reproached Chonghuan, saying: “When two states make peace, the boundaries ought to be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In a second message he rebuked Chonghuan: “Allies fix their borders.

sentences.zh: 今又修葺域垣，潛圖侵逼。

translations.literal: Now again you repair your walls and secretly plot encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: You rebuild your ramparts and plot invasion in secret.

sentences.zh: 倘戰爭不息，天以燕、雲畀我，爾主不幸奔竄，身敗名裂，為何如也。

translations.literal: If war does not cease, Heaven may give Yan and Yun to us; your lord, unlucky, may flee in disgrace, body ruined and name shattered — what then?
translations.idiomatic: If fighting continues, Heaven may hand Yan and Yun to us; your emperor may flee in ruin, his name disgraced forever—consider that.

sentences.zh: 自古文臣不更事者徒為大言，每喪師殃民，社稷傾覆。

translations.literal: From antiquity, civil officials inexperienced in affairs have only uttered grand words, and each time armies were lost and the people afflicted, the altars of state overturned.
translations.idiomatic: History shows that bookish ministers who never smelled battle love grand phrases—and each time, armies perish, peasants suffer, and dynasties fall.

sentences.zh: 前者遼左任用非人，而河東西土地盡失，今尚謂不足戒而謀動干戈耶？

translations.literal: Formerly in Liaodong the wrong men were employed, and the lands east and west of the river were entirely lost — do you still say there is insufficient warning and plot to stir up war?
translations.idiomatic: The Ming already lost everything east of the Liao because the wrong men held command—do you truly see no lesson in that, and still reach for the sword?”

sentences.zh: 」癸丑，阿敏等自朝鮮凱旋，上迎於武靖營，賜阿敏御衣一襲，餘各賜馬一匹。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Amin and the rest returned in triumph from Korea; the Emperor welcomed them at Wujing Camp and bestowed on Amin one suit of imperial robes; the rest each received one horse.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day Amin’s victorious column returned from Korea; Huang Taiji met them at Wujing Camp, gave Amin an imperial robe, and awarded every other officer a horse.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，論征朝鮮將士功，擢賞有差。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, the merit of the officers and soldiers in the Korean campaign was assessed and promotions and rewards were graded.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day he reviewed the Korean campaign honors and promoted or rewarded each man according to his deeds.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，上還瀋陽。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, the Emperor returned to Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day he was back in Mukden.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以書諭察哈爾台吉濟農及奈曼袞出斯巴圖魯來和。

translations.literal: On the day yichou, letters were sent summoning the Chakhar taiji Jinong and the Naiman Günüsibaatur to make peace.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day he wrote to the Chakhar taiji Jinong and to Günüsibaatur of the Naiman, inviting them to submit.

sentences.zh: 五月戊辰，遣朝鮮國王弟李覺歸國，設宴餞之，並賜鞍馬裘帶等物。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day wuchen, the younger brother of the King of Korea, Li Jue, was sent home; a farewell feast was set and saddles, horses, fur coats, belts, and the like were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on wuchen day, he sent King Li Zong’s brother Li Jue home with a parting banquet and gifts of saddles, horses, furs, and belts.

sentences.zh: 辛未，上聞明人於錦州、大凌河、小凌河築城屯田，而崇煥無報書，親率師往攻之。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, the Emperor heard that the Ming were building cities and opening fields at Jinzhou, Dalinghe, and Xiaolinghe, while Chonghuan sent no reply; he personally led the army to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day, learning that the Ming were fortifying Jinzhou, Dalinghe, and Xiaolinghe while Chonghuan remained silent, Huang Taiji took the field in person.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，至廣寧，乘夜進兵。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, he reached Guangning and advanced the army by night.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day he reached Guangning and marched forward under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 丙子，明大凌河、小凌河兵棄城遁，遂圍錦州。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, the Ming troops of Dalinghe and Xiaolinghe abandoned their cities and fled; he then invested Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day the Ming garrisons at Dalinghe and Xiaolinghe abandoned their posts; he laid siege to Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 明台堡兵二千餘人來降，悉縱之歸。

translations.literal: More than two thousand Ming troops from the outlying forts came to surrender; all were released and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Over two thousand Ming soldiers from satellite forts surrendered and were sent home unharmed.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，明鎮守遼東太監紀用、總兵趙率教遣人詣師請命。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, Ji Yong, Ming superintendent of eastern Liaodong, and the commander Zhao Shuaijiao sent men to the army to beg for orders.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day the Ming eunuch Ji Yong and General Zhao Shuaijiao sent envoys to sue for terms.

sentences.zh: 上開誠諭之，並許紀用親來定議。

translations.literal: The Emperor spoke to them openly and in good faith, and also permitted Ji Yong to come in person to fix the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Taiji received them frankly and even invited Ji Yong to come himself to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 用不答，遂攻錦州。

translations.literal: Ji Yong did not answer; the attack on Jinzhou was then pressed.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Yong never came; the assault on Jinzhou resumed.

sentences.zh: 垂克，明援兵至，退五里而營，遣人調瀋陽兵益師。

translations.literal: When the city was on the verge of falling, Ming relief troops arrived; the army withdrew five li and encamped, and men were sent to Mukden to call up reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: As the walls were about to give way, Ming relief appeared; Huang Taiji drew off five li, made camp, and summoned more troops from Mukden.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，固山額真博爾晉等以兵至。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, the gushan ejen Boringjin and others arrived with troops.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day Boringjin and the other banner commanders arrived with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，攻寧遠城，殲其步卒千餘人。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, Ningyuan was attacked and more than a thousand of its foot soldiers were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day he struck Ningyuan and cut down more than a thousand foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 既，明總兵滿桂出城而陣，上欲擊之，三大貝勒均諫止。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Ming commander Man Gui deployed outside the city in battle array; the Emperor wished to strike him, but the three great beile all remonstrated and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Ming general Man Gui drew up his line outside the walls. Huang Taiji meant to charge, but the three senior beile pleaded against it.

sentences.zh: 上怒，趣諸將戴兜鍪，率阿濟格疾馳而進，敗其前隊，追至寧遠城下，盡殪之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, angry, urged the generals to don their helmets; leading Ajige he galloped swiftly forward, defeated their vanguard, pursued to below the walls of Ningyuan, and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, he ordered every commander into his helm, took Ajige, and swept forward at a gallop, shattering the Ming van and chasing the survivors to the very foot of Ningyuan’s walls until none were left.

sentences.zh: 諸貝勒不及冑而從，濟爾哈朗、薩哈廉、瓦克達俱被創。

translations.literal: The beile had not time to arm themselves before they followed; Jirgalang, Sahalian, and Wakda were all wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Other princes rode after him before they could arm; Jirgalang, Sahalian, and Wakda were all wounded in the melée.

sentences.zh: 錦州守兵亦出城合戰，我軍復迎擊之。

translations.literal: The Jinzhou garrison also came out to join battle; our army again met and struck them.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhou’s garrison sallied forth as well, and the Qing host turned to beat them back.

sentences.zh: 游擊覺羅拜山、備御巴希陣歿，上臨其喪，哭而酹之。

translations.literal: The guerrilla officer Gioro Baishan and the defending officer Bashi fell in the line; the Emperor came to their funeral, wept, and poured libation.
translations.idiomatic: The guerrilla Gioro Baishan and the garrison officer Bashi were killed in the fighting; Huang Taiji came to their bier, wept, and poured wine for the dead.

sentences.zh: 我軍還駐雙樹舖。

translations.literal: Our army withdrew and encamped at Shuangshupu.
translations.idiomatic: The army then withdrew to camp at Shuangshupu.

sentences.zh: 乙未，復至錦州。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, they again reached Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day they were before Jinzhou once more.

sentences.zh: 六月己亥，攻錦州，值天溽暑，士卒死傷甚眾。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day jihai, Jinzhou was attacked; the weather was sweltering and troops died and were wounded in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jihai day, the siege of Jinzhou resumed; the heat was brutal and casualties mounted.

sentences.zh: 庚子，班師。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day he ordered the retreat.

sentences.zh: 丁未，上還瀋陽。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, the Emperor returned to Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day he returned to Mukden.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大饑，斗米值銀八兩，銀賤物貴，盜賊繁興。

translations.literal: That year there was great famine; a dou of grain was worth eight taels of silver; silver was cheap and goods dear; bandits flourished.
translations.idiomatic: That year famine gripped the land—a peck of grain cost eight taels of silver, metal was cheap and grain dear, and robbery spread.

sentences.zh: 上惻然曰：「民饑為盜，可盡殺乎！

translations.literal: The Emperor, moved with compassion, said: “When the people hunger they become bandits — can they all be killed?
translations.idiomatic: Moved to pity, he said, “Hungry men steal—must we slaughter them all?”

sentences.zh: 」令鞭而釋之，仍發帑賑民。

translations.literal: He ordered them flogged and released, and still opened the treasury to relieve the people.
translations.idiomatic: He had thieves flogged and freed, and opened the treasury to feed the starving.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己巳，蒙古敖漢瑣諾木杜稜、塞臣卓禮克圖、奈曼袞出斯巴圖魯舉國來附。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day jisi, Sonom Düreng of the Mongol Aohan, Saicinn Jorčitu, and Günüsibaatur of the Naiman came with their entire peoples to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on jisi day, Sonom Düreng of the Aohan Mongols, Saicinn Jorčitu, and Günüsibaatur of the Naiman submitted with their whole tribes.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮國王李倧遣使報謝，並獻方物，命阿什達爾漢等往報之，尋以義州歸朝鮮。

translations.literal: The King of Korea, Li Zong, sent envoys to express thanks and present local products; Ashadahan and others were ordered to go to report in return; shortly Uiju was returned to Korea.
translations.idiomatic: King Li Zong sent thanks and tribute; Huang Taiji dispatched Ashadahan to answer him and soon restored Uiju to Korean control.

sentences.zh: 是月，明袁崇煥罷歸。

translations.literal: That month, Yuan Chonghuan of the Ming was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: That same month the Ming dismissed Yuan Chonghuan from office.

sentences.zh: 八月辛亥，察哈爾阿喇克綽忒部貝勒巴爾巴圖魯、諾門達賚、吹爾扎木蘇率眾來歸。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day xinhai, the Chakhar Alakötü beile Balbatu, Nomendai, and Cuirjambsu led the multitude to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinhai day, the Chakhar beile Balbatu, Nomendai, and Cuirjambsu of the Alakötü came in with their followers.

sentences.zh: 是月，明熹宗崩，其弟信王嗣位，是為莊烈帝。

translations.literal: That month, Ming Xizong died; his younger brother the Prince of Xin succeeded to the throne—this is the Zhuanglie Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Ming emperor Xizong (Tianqi) died. His younger brother, the Prince of Xin, took the throne and is known as the Zhuanglie Emperor (Chongzhen).

sentences.zh: 九月甲子朔，諭國家大祀大宴用牛外，其屠宰馬騾牛驢者悉禁之。

translations.literal: Ninth month, first day (jiazi cyclical), edict: apart from oxen used for the state's great sacrifices and great banquets, all slaughter of horses, mules, cattle, and donkeys is forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month an edict declared that, save for oxen required for state sacrifices and grand feasts, the slaughter of horses, mules, cattle, and donkeys was forbidden throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月庚午，察哈爾大貝勒昂坤杜稜來降。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, gengwu day, Chakhar grand beile Angkun Duling came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter, on the gengwu day, Angkun Duling, grand beile of the Chakhar, submitted.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，薩哈爾察部來朝貢。

translations.literal: Xinsi day, the Sahalcha tribe came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day the Sahalcha tribe presented tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲午朔，察哈爾阿喇克綽忒貝勒圖爾濟伊爾登來降。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, first day (jiawu cyclical), Chakhar Alakchuut beile Tuerji Yierdeng came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month Tuerji Yierdeng, beile of the Chakhar Alakchuut, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月戊子，格伊克裡部長四人率其屬來朝。

translations.literal: Second year, spring, first month, wuzi day, four chiefs of the Geikeli tribe came to court with their followers.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the second year, on the wuzi day, four chiefs of the Geikeli tribe arrived at court with their dependents.

sentences.zh: 二月癸巳朔，以額亦都子圖爾格、費英東子察哈尼俱為總兵官。

translations.literal: Second month, first day (guisi cyclical), Eidu’s son Turgai and Fei Yingdong’s son Chahani were both made commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the second month Turgai, son of Eidu, and Chahani, son of Fei Yingdong, were each appointed commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮國王李倧遣其總兵官李蘭等來獻方物，並米二千石，更以一千石在中江平糶。

translations.literal: The king of Korea, Li Zun, sent his commander Li Lan and others to present local products, and also two thousand piculs of rice; a further thousand piculs were to be sold at fair price on the Zhongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: King Li Zun of Korea sent his commander Li Lan and others with tribute goods and two thousand piculs of rice, with another thousand piculs to be sold at regulated price on the Zhongjiang River.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以往喀喇沁使臣屢為察哈爾多羅特部所殺，上率師親征。

translations.literal: Gengzi day, because envoys to the Kharachin had repeatedly been killed by the Chakhar Dorot tribe, the Emperor led the army in person on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day, after Kharachin envoys had been killed again and again by the Chakhar Dorot, the Emperor took the field in person.

sentences.zh: 丁未，進擊多羅特部，敗之，多爾濟哈談巴圖魯被創遁，獲其妻子，殺台吉古魯，俘萬一千二百人還。

translations.literal: Dingwei day, advanced to attack the Dorot tribe, defeated them; Dorji Khatan Baturu was wounded and fled; his wife and children were captured; Taiji Guru was killed; eleven thousand two hundred persons were taken prisoner and the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day he struck the Dorot, routed them, and wounded Dorji Khatan Baturu, who fled. The Emperor seized his family, slew Taiji Guru, and returned with eleven thousand two hundred captives.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以戰勝，用八牛祭天。

translations.literal: Dingsi day, because of victory, eight oxen were used to sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day, in thanks for victory, he offered sacrifice to Heaven with eight oxen.

sentences.zh: 三月戊辰，上還瀋陽，貝勒阿敏等率群臣郊迎，行抱見禮。

translations.literal: Third month, wuchen day, the Emperor returned to Shenyang; beile Amin and others led the civil and military officials to meet him in the suburbs, performing the embrace-and-see rite.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the third month the Emperor came back to Shenyang. Beile Amin and the officials welcomed him outside the walls with the embrace-and-audience ceremony.

sentences.zh: 以弟多爾袞、多鐸從征有功，賜多爾袞號墨爾根戴青，多鐸號額爾克楚虎爾。

translations.literal: Because his younger brothers Dorgon and Dodo had merit on campaign, Dorgon was granted the title Mergen Daiqing and Dodo the title Erke Chuhor.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Dorgon and Dodo had distinguished themselves on campaign; Dorgon received the title Mergen Daiqing and Dodo the title Erke Chuhor.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以賜名之禮宴之。

translations.literal: Gengyin day, he feasted them with the rites due to the bestowal of names.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day he held a feast for them according to the ritual of granting honorific names.

sentences.zh: 戊子，給國人無妻者金，使娶。

translations.literal: Wuzi day, gold was given to men of the state without wives, so that they might marry.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day he distributed gold to unmarried men of the realm so they could take wives.

sentences.zh: 以貝勒多爾袞為固山貝勒。

translations.literal: Beile Dorgon was made gushan beile.
translations.idiomatic: Beile Dorgon was appointed gushan beile (Banner Prince).

sentences.zh: 夏四月丙辰，巴林貝勒塞特爾，台吉塞冷、阿玉石、滿硃習禮率眾來歸。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, bingchen day, Bairin beile Setter, and the taiji Seler, Ayushi, and Manzhuxili led their peoples to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the bingchen day, Bairin beile Setter and the taiji Seler, Ayushi, and Manzhuxili came over with their followers.

sentences.zh: 明復以袁崇煥督師薊、遼。

translations.literal: The Ming again appointed Yuan Chonghuan to supervise the Ji and Liao fronts.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming once more put Yuan Chonghuan in charge of the Ji and Liao theaters.

sentences.zh: 崇煥素弗善毛文龍。

translations.literal: Chonghuan had never been on good terms with Mao Wenlong.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghuan and Mao Wenlong had long been at odds.

sentences.zh: 時文龍據皮島，招集遼民，有逃亡則殺以冒功，遂得擢總兵，便宜行事。

translations.literal: At that time Wenlong held Pi Island, gathered Liaodong refugees, and when fugitives appeared killed them to claim merit; he thus rose to commander with discretionary powers.
translations.idiomatic: Wenlong then held Pi Island, drew Liaodong refugees to him, and killed runaways to inflate his reports, until he was promoted to regional commander with full discretion.

sentences.zh: 後更致書與我通好。

translations.literal: Later he also sent letters to us seeking friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: He later sent letters proposing friendship with our court.

sentences.zh: 上遣科廓等賚書往報。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Ke Kuo and others bearing letters in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor dispatched Ke Kuo and others with a written reply.

sentences.zh: 既，文龍執科廓等送燕京。

translations.literal: Thereafter Wenlong seized Ke Kuo and the rest and sent them to Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Wenlong then seized Ke Kuo’s party and sent them to the Ming capital.

sentences.zh: 崇煥以文龍私通罪紿殺之。

translations.literal: Chonghuan, on the charge of Wenlong’s private communication with us, deceived and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghuan, citing Wenlong’s secret dealings with us, lured him to his death.

sentences.zh: 五月辛未，明人棄錦州。

translations.literal: Fifth month, xinwei day, the Ming abandoned Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day of the fifth month the Ming gave up Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 貝勒阿巴泰等率兵三千略其地，隳錦州、杏山、高橋三城，毀十三站以東墩台二十一。

translations.literal: Beile Abatai and others led three thousand troops to raid the region, destroyed the three cities Jinzhou, Xingshan, and Gaoqiao, and demolished twenty-one beacon towers east of the thirteen stations.
translations.idiomatic: Beile Abatai and others led three thousand men to ravage the district, razed Jinzhou, Xingshan, and Gaoqiao, and tore down twenty-one beacon towers east of the thirteen relay stations.

sentences.zh: 先是顧特塔布囊以其眾自察哈爾逃匿蒙古地，遇歸附者輒殺之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gurt Tabunang had fled with his people from the Chakhar into Mongol lands and killed those who came to submit whenever he met them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Gurt Tabunang had fled from the Chakhar into Mongolia with his band and slaughtered refugees who sought to join us.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，命貝勒濟爾哈朗、豪格率兵討顧特塔布囊。

translations.literal: Xinsi day, beile Jirhalang and Hooge were ordered to lead troops against Gurt Tabunang.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day beile Jirhalang and Hooge were sent to punish Gurt Tabunang.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，顧特伏誅，俘其人口牲畜以萬計。

translations.literal: Yiyou day, Gurt was executed; people and livestock taken numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day Gurt was put to death, and captives and herds seized ran into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 長白山迤東濱海虎爾哈部頭目裡佛塔等來朝。

translations.literal: Headmen of the Jurchen along the coast east of the Changbai Mountains, including Lifta, came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal Jurchen chiefs east of the Changbai Mountains, led by Lifta, presented themselves at court.

sentences.zh: 八月辛卯，與喀喇沁部議和定盟。

translations.literal: Eighth month, xinmao day, peace and alliance were settled with the Kharachin.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day of the eighth month a treaty of peace and alliance was concluded with the Kharachin.

sentences.zh: 乙未，賜奈曼貝勒袞出斯號達爾漢，札魯特喀巴海號衛徵。

translations.literal: Yiwei day, Naiman beile Gunbushi was granted the title Darhan, and Jarud Kabai the title Weizheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei day Naiman beile Gunbushi received the title Darhan and Jarud Kabai the title Weizheng.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，朝鮮來貢。

translations.literal: Yimao day, Korea sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day Korea presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 九月庚申，徵外籓兵共征蒙古察哈爾。

translations.literal: Ninth month, gengshen day, troops of the outer banners were levied for a joint campaign against the Mongol Chakhar.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the ninth month allied forces from the outer banners were called up for a campaign against the Chakhar Mongols.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，上率大軍西發。

translations.literal: Guihai day, the Emperor led the great army west.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day the Emperor marched west at the head of the main host.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，次遼陽。

translations.literal: Bingyin day, halted at Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day the army encamped at Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 敖漢、奈曼、喀爾喀、札魯特、喀喇沁諸貝勒、台吉各以兵來會。

translations.literal: Aohan, Naiman, Khalkha, Jarud, and Kharachin beile and taiji each came with troops to join.
translations.idiomatic: Beile and taiji of the Aohan, Naiman, Khalkha, Jarud, and Kharachin came in turn with their contingents.

sentences.zh: 己巳，駐師綽洛郭爾。

translations.literal: Jisi day, the army encamped at Chuoluoguoer.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day the host halted at Chuoluoguoer.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，宴來會諸貝勒。

translations.literal: Jiaxu day, a banquet was given for the beile who had come to join.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day he feasted the allied beile.

sentences.zh: 科爾沁諸貝勒不至。

translations.literal: The Khorchin beile did not come.
translations.idiomatic: The Khorchin beile failed to appear.

sentences.zh: 土謝圖汗額駙奧巴、哈談巴圖魯、滿硃習禮如約，請先侵掠而後合軍。

translations.literal: Tüsiyetü Khan’s son-in-law Ooba, Khatan Baturu, and Manzhuxili, as agreed, asked to raid first and then unite the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Ooba, son-in-law of the Tüsiyetü Khan, with Khatan Baturu and Manzhuxili, asked leave to harry the enemy before the main forces joined, as previously arranged.

sentences.zh: 上怒，遣使趣之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and sent envoys to urge them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was displeased and dispatched messengers to hurry them.

sentences.zh: 時奧巴違命，逕歸。

translations.literal: At that time Ooba disobeyed orders and went straight home.
translations.idiomatic: Ooba then defied his orders and withdrew homeward.

sentences.zh: 滿硃習禮及台吉巴敦以所俘來獻，上賜滿硃習禮號達爾漢巴圖魯，巴敦號達爾漢卓禮克圖，厚賚之。

translations.literal: Manzhuxili and taiji Badun presented captives they had taken; the Emperor granted Manzhuxili the title Darhan Baturu and Badun the title Darhan Joriktu, and richly rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: Manzhuxili and taiji Badun brought in prisoners; the Emperor gave Manzhuxili the title Darhan Baturu and Badun Darhan Joriktu, with generous gifts besides.

sentences.zh: 丙子，進兵擊席爾哈、席伯圖、英、湯圖諸處，克之，獲人畜無算。

translations.literal: Bingzi day, the army advanced against Xierha, Xibotu, Ying, Tangtu, and other places, took them, and captured people and livestock beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day he attacked Xierha, Xibotu, Ying, Tangtu, and neighboring posts, seized them, and took booty in men and herds beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛卯，還師。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, xinmao day, the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the xinmao day, the army marched home.

sentences.zh: 丙申，諭敖漢、奈曼、巴林、札魯特諸貝勒，毋得要殺降人，違者科罰。

translations.literal: Bingshen day, edict to the Aohan, Naiman, Bairin, and Jarud beile: do not on any account kill those who surrender; violators will be punished.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day he warned the Aohan, Naiman, Bairin, and Jarud beile that surrendered peoples must not be slaughtered, on pain of penalty.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，上還瀋陽。

translations.literal: Renyin day, the Emperor returned to Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day the Emperor came back to Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 以劉興祚詐稱縊死，逃歸明，繫其母及妻子於獄。

translations.literal: Because Liu Xingzuo had feigned hanging himself and fled back to the Ming, his mother, wife, and children were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xingzuo had pretended suicide and escaped to the Ming; his mother, wife, and children were therefore cast into prison.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁亥朔，遺土謝圖汗額駙奧巴書，數其罪。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, first day (dinghai cyclical), a letter was sent to Tüsiyetü Khan’s son-in-law Ooba enumerating his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month a letter was sent to Ooba, son-in-law of the Tüsiyetü Khan, listing his offenses.

sentences.zh: 巴牙喇部長伊爾彪等來朝貢。

translations.literal: Bayara chief Yierbiao and others came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Yierbiao of the Bayara and others presented tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 蒙古郭畀爾圖、札魯特貝勒塞本及其弟馬尼各率部來歸。

translations.literal: Mongols Guobieritu, Jarud beile Saiben, and his younger brother Mani each led their tribes to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongols Guobieritu, Jarud beile Saiben, and Saiben’s brother Mani each brought their peoples to submit.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月庚申，土謝圖汗奧巴來請罪，宥而遣之。

translations.literal: Third year, spring, first month, gengshen day, Tüsiyetü Khan Ooba came to beg pardon; he was forgiven and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the third year, on the gengshen day, Ooba of the Tüsiyetü Khan came to plead guilt; the Emperor pardoned him and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 辛未，敕科爾沁、敖漢、奈曼、喀爾喀、喀喇沁諸部悉遵國制。

translations.literal: Xinwei day, the Khorchin, Aohan, Naiman, Khalkha, and Kharachin tribes were all ordered to follow the national institutions.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day the Khorchin, Aohan, Naiman, Khalkha, and Kharachin were commanded to observe the laws of the state.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，諭諸貝勒代理三大貝勒直月機務。

translations.literal: Dingchou day, edict to the beile to share in turn the monthly duties of the three great beile.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day he instructed the beile to take turns assisting the three great beile in monthly administration.

sentences.zh: 二月戊子，諭三大貝勒、諸貝勒、大臣毋得科斂民間財物，犯者治罪。

translations.literal: Second month, wuzi day, edict to the three great beile, all beile, and great ministers not to levy goods from the people; offenders will be punished.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day of the second month he forbade the three great beile, the beile, and senior ministers to exact goods from the populace, under penalty of law.

sentences.zh: 己亥，合葬太祖高皇帝、孝慈高皇后於瀋陽之石嘴頭山，妃富察氏祔。

translations.literal: Jihai day, the Taizu Gaohuangdi and Empress Xiaoci Gaohuanghou were interred together at Shizui Mountain in Shenyang; consort Fuca was enshrined with them.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day the Taizu and Empress Xiaoci were buried together at Shizui Mountain near Shenyang, with Consort Fuca placed in the same tomb.

sentences.zh: 喀爾喀札魯特貝勒戴青、桑土、桑古爾、桑噶爾寨等率眾來附。

translations.literal: Khalkha Jarud beile Daiqing, Sangtu, Sanggur, and Sanggaerzhai and others led their peoples to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Khalkha Jarud beile Daiqing, Sangtu, Sanggur, Sanggaerzhai, and others came over with their followers.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，上南巡，閱邊境城堡，圮薄者修築之。

translations.literal: Jiachen day, the Emperor toured south, inspected border forts, and repaired those whose walls were ruined or thin.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day he made a southern tour, examined frontier strongholds, and rebuilt any whose defenses had crumbled or thinned.

sentences.zh: 戊申，次海州，有老人年一百三歲，妻一百五歲，子七十三歲，召見賜牛種。

translations.literal: Wushen day, halted at Haizhou; an old man of one hundred three, his wife one hundred five, and their son seventy-three were summoned, seen, and given cattle and seed.
translations.idiomatic: At Haizhou on the wushen day he received a household of extraordinary age—a man of one hundred three, his wife one hundred five, their son seventy-three—and bestowed cattle and seed.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，上還瀋陽。

translations.literal: Xinhai day, the Emperor returned to Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day the Emperor returned to Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 三月戊午，申蒙古諸部軍令。

translations.literal: Third month, wuwu day, military regulations for the Mongol tribes were proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day of the third month he issued army regulations for the Mongol tribes.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丙戌朔，設文館，命巴克什達海及剛林等繙譯漢字書籍，庫爾纏及吳巴什等記注本朝政事。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, first day (bingxu cyclical), the Literary Office was established; Bakshi Dahai and Ganglin and others were ordered to translate Chinese books, and Kuerchan and Wubashi and others to record the affairs of the present dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month of summer he founded the Literary Office, charging Dahai, Ganglin, and their colleagues with translating Chinese texts and Kuerchan, Wubashi, and others with compiling the annals of the reign.

sentences.zh: 五月丁未，奈曼、札魯特諸貝勒越界駐牧，自請議罰。

translations.literal: Fifth month, dingwei day, Naiman and Jarud beile pastured across the border and asked of their own accord to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day of the fifth month Naiman and Jarud beile who had grazed beyond their bounds volunteered to accept punishment.

sentences.zh: 上宥之。

translations.literal: The Emperor pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor granted them pardon.

sentences.zh: 六月乙丑，議伐明，令科爾沁、喀爾喀、札魯特、敖漢、奈曼諸部會兵，並令預采木造船以備轉餉。

translations.literal: Sixth month, yichou day, an expedition against the Ming was debated; the Khorchin, Khalkha, Jarud, Aohan, and Naiman tribes were ordered to muster, and also to gather timber in advance and build boats to prepare for transport of provisions.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day of the sixth month he resolved on war with the Ming, calling the Khorchin, Khalkha, Jarud, Aohan, and Naiman to arms and ordering them to cut timber and build boats for supply lines.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，喀喇沁布爾噶都戴青、台吉卓爾畢，土默特台吉阿玉石等遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Dingmao day, Kharachin Burgudut Daiqing, taiji Jorbi, and Tümed taiji Ayushi and others sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day Burgudut Daiqing of the Kharachin, taiji Jorbi, Tümed taiji Ayushi, and others sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，土默特台吉卓爾畢泰等來朝貢。

translations.literal: Xinsi day, Tümed taiji Jorbitai and others came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day Tümed taiji Jorbitai and others presented tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 秋七月辛卯，喀爾喀台吉拜渾岱、喇巴泰、滿硃習禮自科爾沁來朝。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, xinmao day, Khalkha taiji Baihundai, Labatai, and Manzhuxili came from the Khorchin to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the xinmao day, Khalkha taiji Baihundai, Labatai, and Manzhuxili arrived from the Khorchin.

sentences.zh: 甲午，孟阿圖率兵征瓦爾喀。

translations.literal: Jiawu day, Mengatu led troops against the Warka.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day Mengatu marched against the Warka.

sentences.zh: 乙未，庫爾喀部來朝貢。

translations.literal: Yiwei day, the Kurka tribe sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei day the Kurka tribe presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 八月庚午，頒八旗臨陣賞罰令。

translations.literal: Eighth month, gengwu day, regulations on rewards and punishments for the Eight Banners in battle were promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day of the eighth month he issued the Eight Banners’ regulations for reward and punishment on campaign.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，諭曰：「自古及今，文武並用，以文治世，以武克敵。

translations.literal: Yihai day, edict: "From antiquity to the present, civil and military are used together—civil to govern the realm, military to overcome the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day he proclaimed: "From antiquity onward civil and military arts have gone together: learning to govern the realm, arms to defeat the enemy."

sentences.zh: 今欲振興文教，試錄生員。

translations.literal: Now wishing to revive civil culture and instruction, licentiates are to be examined.
translations.idiomatic: "We now intend to revive literary culture and will hold examinations for licentiates."

sentences.zh: 諸貝勒府及滿、漢、蒙古所有生員，俱令赴試。

translations.literal: Licentiates in the households of all beile and among Manchu, Han, and Mongol are all ordered to come for examination.
translations.idiomatic: "Every licentiate in the beile’s establishments and among Manchu, Han, and Mongol subjects must present himself for the test."

sentences.zh: 中式者以他丁償之。

translations.literal: Those who pass will have corvée service compensated by another ding.
translations.idiomatic: "Those who pass shall have their labor obligations transferred to another household."

sentences.zh: 九月壬午朔，初試生員，拔二百人，賞緞布有差，免其差徭。

translations.literal: Ninth month, first day (renwu cyclical), the first licentiate examination was held; two hundred were selected, rewarded with satin and cloth in differing grades, and exempted from corvée.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month the first licentiate examination was held. Two hundred candidates passed, received graded gifts of satin and cloth, and were freed from corvée.

sentences.zh: 癸未，貝勒濟爾哈朗等略明錦州、寧遠諸路還，俘獲以三千計。

translations.literal: Guiwei day, beile Jirhalang and others raided the Ming routes of Jinzhou and Ningyuan and returned; captives numbered about three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day beile Jirhalang and others returned from raiding Jinzhou and Ningyuan, with some three thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，阿魯部杜思噶爾濟農始遣使來通好。

translations.literal: Bingxu day, the Aru Dusigal jinong first sent envoys to open friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingxu day the Aru Dusigal jinong sent his first embassy seeking friendship.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，喀喇沁布爾噶都來朝貢。

translations.literal: Guimao day, Kharachin Burgudu came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day Burgudu of the Kharachin presented tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 冬十月癸丑，上親征明，徵蒙古諸部兵以次來會。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, guichou day, the Emperor campaigned against the Ming in person; Mongol tribes were to bring troops in succession to join.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the guichou day, the Emperor took the field against the Ming in person, summoning Mongol levies to assemble in turn.

sentences.zh: 庚申，次納裡特河，察哈爾五千人來歸。

translations.literal: Gengshen day, halted at the Nalite River; five thousand Chakhar came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day the host encamped on the Nalite River, where five thousand Chakhar surrendered.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，次遼河。

translations.literal: Renxu day, halted at the Liao River.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day the army halted on the Liao River.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，科爾沁奧巴以二十三貝勒來會。

translations.literal: Bingyin day, Khorchin Ooba came to join with twenty-three beile.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day Ooba of the Khorchin arrived with twenty-three beile.

sentences.zh: 上集諸貝勒大臣議征明與征察哈爾孰利，皆言察哈爾遠，於是征明。

translations.literal: The Emperor assembled beile and ministers to discuss whether attacking the Ming or the Chakhar was more profitable; all said the Chakhar were distant, and so they campaigned against the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor convened beile and ministers to weigh war on the Ming against war on the Chakhar. All held the Chakhar too remote, and the march turned toward the Ming.

sentences.zh: 辛未，次喀喇沁之青城。

translations.literal: Xinwei day, halted at the Green City of the Kharachin.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day the army encamped at the Kharachin Green City.

sentences.zh: 大貝勒代善、三貝勒莽古爾泰止諸貝勒帳外，入見密議班師。

translations.literal: Grand beile Daishan and third beile Manggūltai kept the other beile outside the tent and entered alone to discuss withdrawal in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Grand beile Daishan and third beile Manggūltai left the other beile outside and went in alone to urge a secret retreat.

sentences.zh: 既退，岳託等入白諸將在外候進取。

translations.literal: After they withdrew, Yuetuo and others entered and reported that the generals were waiting outside, expecting to advance.
translations.idiomatic: When they had gone out, Yuetuo and others came in and said the commanders were waiting to press the attack.

sentences.zh: 上不懌，因曰：「兩兄謂我兵深入，勞師襲遠，若糧匱馬疲，敵人環攻，無為歸計。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased and said: "The two elder brothers say my army has penetrated deep; a weary host striking far—if grain runs short and horses tire, and the enemy surrounds and attacks, there will be no plan for return.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was angered and said, "You two tell me the army is deep in enemy country—that a tired force striking far, with grain exhausted and horses spent, may be encircled with no road home.

sentences.zh: 若等見及此，而初不言，朕既遠涉，乃以此為辭。

translations.literal: If you saw this and at first did not speak, I having already marched far—now you use this as your plea.
translations.idiomatic: "If you saw that danger and said nothing until now, when I have already marched so far, you offer it only as an excuse to turn back.

sentences.zh: 我謀且隳，何候為！

translations.literal: My plan is about to be ruined—what are they waiting for!
translations.idiomatic: "My whole design is near ruin—why should anyone still wait?"

sentences.zh: 」岳託堅請進師。

translations.literal: " Yuetuo firmly begged to advance the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuetuo pressed hard for the army to go forward.

sentences.zh: 八固山額真詣代善、莽古爾泰議，夜半議定。

translations.literal: The gushan ejen of the eight banners went to Daishan and Manggūltai to deliberate; at midnight the decision was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The gushan ejen of the Eight Banners conferred with Daishan and Manggūltai, and near midnight a decision was reached.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「朕承天命，興師伐明，拒者戮，降者勿擾。

translations.literal: Edict: "I, bearing Heaven's mandate, raise troops to attack the Ming—those who resist are to be slain, those who surrender are not to be disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed: "I, bearing Heaven’s mandate, march against the Ming. Resisters shall be put to the sword; those who yield shall not be molested.

sentences.zh: 俘獲之人，父母妻子勿使離散。

translations.literal: Among captives, do not separate parents, wives, and children.
translations.idiomatic: "Do not part parents from wives and children among prisoners.

sentences.zh: 勿淫人婦女，勿褫人衣服，勿毀廬舍器皿，勿伐果木，勿酗酒。

translations.literal: Do not violate others' wives, do not strip others' clothing, do not destroy houses and vessels, do not cut down fruit trees, do not drink to excess.
translations.idiomatic: "Do not debauch women, strip the living, wreck houses and goods, fell fruit trees, or drink to drunkenness.

sentences.zh: 違者罪無赦。

translations.literal: Violators are guilty without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: "Whoever breaks these rules is guilty without mercy.

sentences.zh: 固山額真等不禁，罪如之。

translations.literal: Gushan ejen and others who do not restrain them—guilt is the same.
translations.idiomatic: "Gushan ejen who fail to restrain their men share the same guilt."

sentences.zh: 」乙亥，次老河，命濟爾哈朗、岳託率右翼兵攻大安口，阿巴泰、阿濟格率左翼兵攻龍井關。

translations.literal: " Yihai day, halted at the Lao River; Jirhalang and Yuetuo were ordered to lead the right wing against Daankou, Abatai and Ajige the left wing against Longjing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day the army encamped at the Lao River. Jirhalang and Yuetuo were sent with the right wing against Daankou, Abatai and Ajige with the left against Longjing Pass.

sentences.zh: 上與大貝勒代善、三貝勒莽古爾泰率大兵繼之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed with the great beile Daishan and the third beile Manggūltai at the head of the main army.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor came on with the main host behind Daishan and Manggūltai.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，左翼兵克龍井關，明副將易愛、參將王遵臣來援，皆敗死。

translations.literal: Dingchou day: the left wing took Longjing Pass; Ming vice-commander Yi Ai and regional commander Wang Zunchen came to relieve it and were both defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day the left wing seized Longjing Pass. Yi Ai and Wang Zunchen marched to its relief and were cut down.

sentences.zh: 漢兒莊、潘家口守將俱降。

translations.literal: The garrison commanders of Han'erzhuang and Panjiakou all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders of Han'erzhuang and Panjiakou submitted.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，上督兵克洪山口。

translations.literal: Wuyin day: the Emperor personally directed the troops and took Hongshan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day he led the assault and carried Hongshan Pass.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，上至遵化。

translations.literal: Xinsi day: the Emperor reached Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day he arrived before Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 莽古爾泰率左翼兵自漢兒莊來會。

translations.literal: Manggūltai led the left wing from Han'erzhuang to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Manggūltai brought the left wing up from Han'erzhuang to rendezvous.

sentences.zh: 遺書明巡撫王元雅勸降。

translations.literal: He sent a letter urging the Ming provincial commissioner Wang Yuanya to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Wang Yuanya, the Ming governor, urging surrender.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬午朔，右翼諸貝勒率師來會。

translations.literal: First day of the eleventh month (renwu cyclical): the beile of the right wing arrived with their forces.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month the right-wing princes joined the army.

sentences.zh: 先是濟爾哈朗等克大安口，五戰皆捷，降馬蘭營、馬蘭口、大安營三城，明羅文峪守將李思禮降。

translations.literal: Earlier Jirhalang and others had taken Daankou, won five battles, reduced Malan Camp, Malankou, and Daan Camp, and the Ming defender Li Sili of Luowen Valley surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Jirhalang had already stormed Daankou, won five engagements, and taken Malan Camp, Malankou, and Daan Camp; Li Sili, Ming commander at Luowen Valley, had yielded.

sentences.zh: 山海關總兵趙率教以兵四千來援，阿濟格迎擊斬之。

translations.literal: Zhao Lüjiao, Ming commander at Shanhaiguan, came with four thousand troops to relieve them; Ajige met and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lüjiao, regional commander of Shanhaiguan, hurried forward with four thousand men; Ajige intercepted and slew him.

sentences.zh: 甲申，諸貝勒攻遵化，正白旗小校薩木哈圖先登，大兵繼之，遂克其城。

translations.literal: Jiashen day: the beile assaulted Zunhua; Samukhatu, corporal of the Plain White Banner, scaled first, the main army followed, and the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day the princes invested Zunhua. Samukhatu of the Plain White Banner went over the wall first; the main columns poured in and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 明巡撫王元雅自經死。

translations.literal: Wang Yuanya, Ming provincial commissioner, hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wang Yuanya took his own life.

sentences.zh: 上親酌金卮賜薩木哈圖，擢備御，世襲罔替，賜號巴圖魯，有過赦免，家固貧，恤之。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally poured from a golden goblet for Samukhatu, promoted him to guard officer with perpetual hereditary rank, granted the title Baturu, pardon for offenses, and because his family was poor gave him relief.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor himself filled a golden cup for Samukhatu, made him a guard officer with hereditary tenure, named him Baturu, promised forgiveness for future faults, and, finding his household destitute, gave him aid.

sentences.zh: 蒙古兵擾害羅文峪民。

translations.literal: Mongol troops harassed the people of Luowen Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol soldiers preyed on the people of Luowen Valley.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「凡貝勒大臣有掠歸降城堡財物者斬，擅殺降民者抵罪，強取民物，計所取倍償之。

translations.literal: Order: "Any beile or minister who plunders goods from surrendered castles shall be beheaded; anyone who kills surrendered people without authority shall answer for it; anyone who forcibly seizes civilian goods shall repay double what was taken.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed: “Any prince or minister who loots a surrendered town shall die. Anyone who slays surrendered people without orders shall be punished. Anyone who seizes civilian property by force shall repay twice the value.”

sentences.zh: 」己丑，敘克城功，將士賞賚有差。

translations.literal: " Jichou day: rewards for the capture of the city were graded and distributed to officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day he ranked the merit of the siege and rewarded the troops accordingly.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，參將英俄爾岱、文館范文程留守遵化，大軍進逼燕京。

translations.literal: Renchen day: regional commander Ying'orda and the Literary Office's Fan Wencheng were left to hold Zunhua; the main army pressed toward Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day Ying'orda and Fan Wencheng of the Literary Office garrisoned Zunhua while the main host marched on the Ming capital.

sentences.zh: 有蒙古兵殺人而褫其衣，上命射殺之。

translations.literal: Some Mongols killed a man and stripped his clothes; the Emperor ordered them shot.
translations.idiomatic: When Mongols killed a man and stripped him, the Emperor had them executed by bow.

sentences.zh: 甲午，徇薊州。

translations.literal: Jiawu day: marched through Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day the army passed through Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 乙未，徇三河。

translations.literal: Yiwei day: marched through Sanhe.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day it marched through Sanhe.

sentences.zh: 丙申，左翼貝勒赴通州視渡口。

translations.literal: Bingshen day: the left-wing beile went to Tongzhou to reconnoiter the crossing.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day the left-wing princes went to Tongzhou to scout the ford.

sentences.zh: 明大同、宣府二鎮援兵至順義，貝勒阿巴泰、岳託擊敗之。

translations.literal: Ming relief from the Datong and Xuanfu garrisons reached Shunyi; beile Abatai and Yuetuo defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Relief columns from Datong and Xuanfu reached Shunyi; Abatai and Yuetuo routed them.

sentences.zh: 順義降。

translations.literal: Shunyi surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Shunyi submitted.

sentences.zh: 上至通州，諭明士民曰：「我國夙以忠順守邊，葉赫與我同一國耳，明主庇葉赫而陵我，大恨有七。

translations.literal: At Tongzhou the Emperor addressed the Ming populace, saying: "Our state has long kept the frontier in loyal obedience. Yehe and we were one country; the Ming rulers sheltered Yehe and wronged us—there are seven great wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: At Tongzhou he spoke to the Ming people: “Our state has long guarded the border in loyalty. Yehe was of one house with us; your court sheltered Yehe and humbled us—seven grave injuries stand between us.

sentences.zh: 我知終不相容，故告天興師。

translations.literal: I knew we could not long coexist, and therefore appealed to Heaven and raised arms.
translations.idiomatic: “I knew we could not endure together, and so I called on Heaven and took the field.

sentences.zh: 天直我國，賜我河東地。

translations.literal: Heaven upheld our state and granted us the lands east of the river.
translations.idiomatic: “Heaven favored us and gave us the country east of the Liao.

sentences.zh: 我太祖皇帝猶原和好，與民休息。

translations.literal: Our Taizu still wished for peace and rest for the people.
translations.idiomatic: “Taizu still sought peace and ease for the people.

sentences.zh: 爾國不從，天又賜我河西地。

translations.literal: Your state would not agree; Heaven again gave us the lands west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: “Your court refused; Heaven then gave us the lands west of the Liao.

sentences.zh: 及朕即位，復徇爾國之請，遂欲去帝稱汗，趣制國印，而爾國不從。

translations.literal: When I took the throne I again heeded your state's request and was ready to lay aside the imperial title and style myself Khan and hasten the making of a state seal—yet your state would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: “When I succeeded, I again heard your plea and was ready to set aside the title of emperor, call myself Khan, and strike a seal of state—yet you would not agree.

sentences.zh: 今我興師而來，順者撫，逆者誅。

translations.literal: Now I march: those who submit I will cherish; those who resist I will punish.
translations.idiomatic: “Now I come in arms: submit and you shall be spared; resist and you shall be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 是爾君好逞干戈，猶爾之君殺爾也。

translations.literal: It is your ruler who delights in arms—it is as if your ruler were slaying you himself.
translations.idiomatic: “It is your sovereign who loves war—it is your sovereign who kills you.

sentences.zh: 天運循環，無往不復，有天子而為匹夫，亦有匹夫而為天子者。

translations.literal: Heaven's wheel turns; nothing departs that does not return. There are times when a Son of Heaven becomes a common man, and when a common man becomes Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: “Heaven's cycle turns; what goes must come again. A Son of Heaven may become a commoner, and a commoner may become Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 天既佑我，乃使我去帝號。

translations.literal: Heaven having aided us, has caused me to lay aside the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: “Heaven has aided us and made me set aside the title of emperor.

sentences.zh: 天其鑒之！

translations.literal: May Heaven witness this!
translations.idiomatic: “Let Heaven be witness!”

sentences.zh: 」辛丑，大軍逼燕京。

translations.literal: " Xinchou day: the main army pressed Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day the host closed on Beijing.

sentences.zh: 上營於城北土城關之東，兩翼營於東北。

translations.literal: The Emperor encamped east of Tuchengguan north of the city; the wings encamped to the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: He pitched his camp east of Tuchengguan on the north side of the wall; the wings lay to the northeast.

sentences.zh: 明大同總兵滿桂、宣府總兵侯世祿屯德勝門，寧遠巡撫袁崇煥、錦州總兵祖大壽屯沙窩門。

translations.literal: Ming Datong commander Man Gui and Xuanfu commander Hou Shilu held Desheng Gate; Ningyuan commissioner Yuan Chonghuan and Jinzhou commander Zu Dashou held Shawo Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Man Gui of Datong and Hou Shilu of Xuanfu held Desheng Gate; Yuan Chonghuan, governor of Ningyuan, and Zu Dashou of Jinzhou held Shawo Gate.

sentences.zh: 上率右翼大貝勒代善，貝勒濟爾哈朗、岳託、杜度、薩哈廉等，領白甲護軍、蒙古兵進擊桂、世祿，遣左翼大貝勒莽古爾泰、阿巴泰、阿濟格、多爾袞、多鐸、豪格等，領白甲護軍、蒙古兵迎擊崇煥、大壽，俱敗之。

translations.literal: The Emperor led the right-wing great beile Daishan and beile Jirhalang, Yuetuo, Dudu, Sahalian, and others with white-armored guards and Mongols to strike Gui and Shilu; he sent the left-wing great beile Manggūltai, Abatai, Ajige, Dorgon, Dodo, and Hooge with white-armored guards and Mongols against Chonghuan and Dashou; both forces were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He himself, with Daishan and the right-wing princes Jirhalang, Yuetuo, Dudu, and Sahalian, led the white-armored guards and Mongols against Gui and Shilu; Manggūltai, Abatai, Ajige, Dorgon, Dodo, and Hooge with the left wing met Chonghuan and Dashou. Both Ming bodies were beaten.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，遣明歸順王太監賚書與明議和。

translations.literal: Guimao day: the Ming defector eunuch Wang was sent with letters to negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day he sent the surrendered Ming eunuch Wang with letters proposing peace.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，屯南海子。

translations.literal: Yisi day: encamped at Nanhaizi.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day the army encamped at Nanhaizi.

sentences.zh: 戊申，袁崇煥、祖大壽營於城東南隅，樹柵為衛，我軍偪之而營。

translations.literal: Wushen day: Yuan Chonghuan and Zu Dashou camped in the southeast corner of the city, palisaded for defense; our army pressed close and encamped.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day Chonghuan and Dashou entrenched in the southeast corner behind wooden barriers; the Qing host camped hard against them.

sentences.zh: 上率輕騎往視。

translations.literal: The Emperor led light cavalry to reconnoiter.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rode out with a light escort to view the lines.

sentences.zh: 諸貝勒請攻城，諭曰：「路隘且險，若傷我士卒，雖得百城不足多也。

translations.literal: The beile asked to storm the city; he instructed them: "The roads are narrow and steep; if we injure our soldiers, a hundred cities would not make up for it.
translations.idiomatic: The princes urged an assault; he said, “The ground is narrow and steep. If we spend our men here, no gain of a hundred towns would repay the loss.”

sentences.zh: 」因止弗攻。

translations.literal: " and therefore halted the attack.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore forbore the attack.

sentences.zh: 初，獲明太監二人，令副將高鴻中，參將鮑承先、寧完我等受密計。

translations.literal: Earlier two Ming eunuchs had been captured; deputy commander Gao Hongzhong and regional commanders Bao Chengxian, Ning Wanwo, and others were given a secret plan.
translations.idiomatic: Two Ming eunuchs had been taken earlier; Hongzhong, Chengxian, Wanwo, and others were entrusted with a stratagem.

sentences.zh: 至是，鴻中、承先坐近二太監耳語云：「今日撤兵，乃上計也。

translations.literal: At this Hongzhong and Chengxian, seated near the two eunuchs, whispered: "Today's withdrawal is the Emperor's stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Now Hongzhong and Chengxian, sitting close by the eunuchs, murmured, “Today's retreat is the Emperor's design.”

sentences.zh: 頃上單騎向敵，敵二人見上語良久乃去。

translations.literal: Just now the Emperor rode alone toward the enemy; two men met him and spoke at length before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: “A moment ago the Emperor rode alone toward the enemy lines; two men met him and talked long before they parted.”

sentences.zh: 意袁都堂有約，此事就矣。

translations.literal: It seems Commissioner Yuan has an understanding—the affair is settled.
translations.idiomatic: “Commissioner Yuan must have an agreement—the business is done.”

sentences.zh: 」時楊太監佯臥竊聽。

translations.literal: Eunuch Yang feigned sleep and eavesdropped.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Yang pretended to sleep and listened.

sentences.zh: 翌日縱之歸，以所聞語明帝，遂下崇煥於獄。

translations.literal: The next day they were released; what they heard was reported to the Ming emperor, and Chonghuan was thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they were sent back; Yang repeated what he had heard to the Chongzhen emperor, and Chonghuan was cast into prison.

sentences.zh: 大壽懼，率所部奔錦州，毀山海關而出。

translations.literal: Dashou was afraid; he led his troops in flight to Jinzhou, breaking through Shanhaiguan as he went.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou, in fear, broke out toward Jinzhou and forced his way through Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 諸貝勒大臣請攻城，上曰：「攻則可克，但恐傷我良將勁卒，余不忍也。

translations.literal: The beile and ministers again asked to storm the city; the Emperor said: "It could be taken, but I fear injuring our good commanders and crack troops—I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: The princes again begged to storm the walls. The Emperor said, “We could take it, but I will not spend my best commanders and veterans.”

sentences.zh: 」遂止。

translations.literal: " and therefore halted.
translations.idiomatic: He again held back the assault.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛亥朔，大軍經海子而南，且獵且行，趣良鄉，克其城。

translations.literal: First day of the twelfth month (xinhai cyclical): the main army marched south by way of the Haizi, hunting as it went, and pressed toward Liangxiang and took the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month the host turned south past the Haizi, hunting on the march, and seized Liangxiang.

sentences.zh: 壬子，總兵吳訥格克固安。

translations.literal: Renzi day: commander Wu Nage took Gu'an.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day Wu Nage captured Gu'an.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，遣貝勒阿巴泰、薩哈廉以太牢祀金太祖、世宗陵。

translations.literal: Xinyou day: beile Abatai and Sahalian sacrificed with the great victim at the tombs of the Jin founders Taizu and Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day Abatai and Sahalian offered the great sacrifice at the Jin tombs of Taizu and Shizong.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，復趨燕京，敗明兵於盧溝橋，殲其眾。

translations.literal: Bingyin day: again pressed toward Yanjing, defeated Ming troops at the Lugou Bridge, and annihilated their force.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day the army again closed on Beijing, routed the Ming at Lugou Bridge, and destroyed their column.

sentences.zh: 明總兵滿桂、孫祖壽、黑雲龍、麻登雲以兵四萬柵永定門之南。

translations.literal: Ming commanders Man Gui, Sun Zushou, Hei Yunlong, and Ma Dengyun with forty thousand men palisaded south of Yongding Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Man Gui, Sun Zushou, Hei Yunlong, and Ma Dengyun entrenched forty thousand men south of Yongding Gate.

sentences.zh: 丁卯黎明，師毀柵入，斬桂、祖壽及副將以下三十餘人，擒黑雲龍、麻登雲，獲馬六千，分賜將士。

translations.literal: At dawn on dingmao the army tore down the palisade and entered, beheaded Gui, Zushou, and more than thirty officers through vice-commander rank, captured Hei Yunlong and Ma Dengyun, took six thousand horses, and distributed them among the troops.
